scope: Independent read-only diagnosis of isolated File/FormData inspector-versus-wire probe, not actual application upload acceptance
findings: All36 controls contain the exact42expected bytes in DOM input File, chosen File before FormData and actual FormData file immediately before fetch; both input-selected and constructed Files are covered with valid and angle-bracket filenames.

All24 independent HTTP receiver traces (no interception or inspect-and-continue) contain exact42file bytes in raw received body and independently parsed file. All eight WebKit wire cases carry42bytes despite all eight WebKit route inspector parsed files reporting0bytes. Chromium/Firefox inspector and wire both report42.
Inspect-and-fulfill emits no wire request by design, so those twelve traces prove only pre-fetch File/FormData contents and inspector behavior. They must not be counted as actual wire transport.

Within these isolated controls the zero-byte observation is an engine/protocol inspector representation limitation rather than proof of empty native File or failed wire transfer. Filename and input-versus-constructed controls do not change the observed WebKit distinction.
conclusion: Retain failed217V2 unchanged. limits: Probe is app-free and backend-free, using owned token-scoped loopback receiver. It does not establish actual component HTTP wire contents, real XLSX parser acceptance or production upload success.
